headline: There are radio stations that only read out numbers. Some were for spies.
slides: Shortwave stations that broadcast strings of numbers in flat voices, often with a tune or a tone first.
A Russian station on 4625 kHz has buzzed almost nonstop for decades. Nobody has admitted running it.
Shortwave reaches the whole world, and anyone can listen without leaving a trace.
In 2001 the 'Cuban Five' were convicted of spying in the US. They'd decoded messages from a Cuban station, 'Atención'.
Prosecutors said the spies wrote down the numbers from a handheld radio and decoded them on laptops.
Many are still broadcasting. You can listen online right now.
